featured_reviews.name: Gourmet Musafir
featured_reviews.review_text:
After studying at The Culinary Institute of America, working with multiple Michelin star restaurants in New York, Chef Freny Fernandes launched her baby Monèr, a bistro in the day, serving a wide range of savoury items covering breakfast and mains. But post 7:00pm it turns into a contemporary dessert bar serving three to five course plated desserts. The white walls, minimalistic furniture, plush velvet seating in teal & pink will remind you of France.

We tried some savoury delicacies & desserts. To begin with..
1. Gnudi is a gnocchi like dumplings made of ricotta cheese in tomato butter, sage, brown butter, micro greens & pumpkin seeds. It was light and soft but the gravy was bursting with flavours.
2. Beetroot Risotto - a classic creamy Italian rice dish with a not so sweet beetroot taste.
3. Spicy Tropical Sangria - a cocktail inspired by raw mango and topped with jalapeño and tobacco. A super refreshing drink to beat the heat this summer.
4. Dawn in the Meadows - an Italian inspired dessert. Granita made with green apple & zesty keffir lime, meringue kisses, micro greens & pumpkin seeds. The dessert depicts the the first few drops of the day (meringue pieces) on the grass (granita). The minty icy granite is so refreshing, that it sets the palate for the next dessert.
5. Phases of moon - Yummy, crescent shaped vanilla sable, topped with spheres made of 60% chocolate ganache, grey ice-cream & berry compote to give that tangy taste to your buds.
6. Jardin au Rose, a big red rose shaped parfait in the centre and surrounded by…its a raspberry & rose parfait accompanied with pistachio baklava, air cake, chocolate soil & edible flowers. Undoubtedly, it looked splendid and left me reluctant to dig in.

This instagramable place has a wall art themed on la vie en rose. Definitely a must visit place.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The ambience is warm, cosy, and very inviting.

Definitely a place I’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Indulge Creamery Cafe is one of Bandra West’s newest and buzzy café-creamery spots. A hybrid ice-cream creamery + café destination - a concept that blends premium desserts with comforting café fare. The space is bright, stylish & Instagram-friendly - soft pink walls, bold green tiles, mirrored accents, and modern lighting create a playful yet premium feel. It’s designed to have cozy conversations, quick meet-ups, or dessert dates. This cafe open up early morning at 7am serving varities of breakfast options including healthy smoothie bowl and closes till late night 3am that fulfills your dessert urges. The menu is smartly curated with breakfast options to quick bites that goes along with beverages and drinks.
• The ice cream Sundae are a highlight — imaginative, premium-quality scoops with toppings that nod to global inspiration but tailored for Indian tastes. The Strawberry Greek Yogurt Sundae was just awesome and yumm.
• The Mocktails, Milkshakes are rich, indulgent, and often photogenic. Loved its Strawberry Matcha and Citrus Matcha Mojito.
• Artisanal single-origin coffees — thoughtfully sourced and crafted, with espresso, affogato-style drinks, lattes, etc.
• The café side isn’t just desserts but burgers, sandwiches and light bites are on the menu, designed to balance the sweetness. Top comfort eats are Avocado Toast, Pesto Crossiant, Bagel Ceasar Sandwich and Watermelon feta salad — great for pairing with shakes or coffees.
If you want a quiet work-friendly café — this is more about the vibe, visuals, and indulgence.

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hey — thanks for coming by and for taking the time to share your feedback.
We’re genuinely sorry the experience didn’t land for you. That said, a couple of things feel important to clarify.
We always encourage guests to taste as many flavours as they’d like before ordering — so what you finally pick is something you’re confident about. Our gelato isn’t designed to please everyone, especially if you’re used to very sweet, stabiliser-heavy or conventional ice creams. We work with clean, plant-based ingredients and naturally sweetened systems, which results in a very different (and intentional) flavour profile.

On billing — we absolutely provide invoices digitally (via phone/email) as part of our current system. Happy to share one anytime if details are provided.

We do take feedback seriously, but we also stand by what we’re building. It’s not meant to be “for the masses” — it’s meant to be honest, considered, and a little different.

featured_reviews.name: Arzan Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of trying out the desserts from Country Of Origin, and I must say, it was quite an experience. I ordered their desserts for delivery at home, and they did not disappoint.

1. Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse (Very Good):
The first dessert I tried was the Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse, and it was an absolute delight. The dessert featured a thick, buttery caramel sauce with a subtle hint of sea salt, perfectly sandwiched between Country Of Origin's luxurious chocolate mousse. The combination of sweet and salty flavors was on point, and the texture was incredibly smooth and creamy. It left a wonderful lingering taste on my palate, making it a standout dish.

2. Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse (Very Good):
The Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse was another winner. This dessert showcased Country Of Origin's signature dark chocolate mousse infused with the earthy and robust flavor of Turkish coffee. The result was a rich and decadent treat with a bittersweet taste that was simply heavenly. I appreciated the collaboration with Mediterranea, as it added a unique twist to this dessert.

3. Eggless Dark Chocolate Chunk Cookie (OK):
Moving on to the Eggless Dark Chocolate Chunk Cookie, I have to admit that it didn't quite live up to the high standard set by the previous desserts. While it was good, it fell into the "okay" category for me. The cookie had a nice, deep chocolate flavor, and the chunks of dark chocolate were a definite plus. However, it lacked that soft, gooey texture that makes cookies truly exceptional.

4. Eggless Caramelized Cashew Nuts (OK):
Similarly, the Eggless Caramelized Cashew Nuts were also in the "okay" range. These nuts had a good caramelized sweetness to them, but they didn't stand out as much as the mousse desserts did. They provided a nice crunch, but I was hoping for a bit more of a caramelized punch in the flavour.

In conclusion, Country Of Origin's desserts truly shine in the mousse category. The Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse and the Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse were exceptional, offering a symphony of flavors and textures that left me craving more. While the cookies and caramelized cashew nuts were decent, they didn't quite reach the same level of excellence. I would highly recommend trying out the mousse desserts if you have the chance, whether dining in at the restaurant or ordering them for delivery – they are a sweet indulgence worth savoring.
